import pandas as pd

# File paths for source CSV files
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_37/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_37/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_37/training_2.csv"
source3_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_37/training_3.csv"

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)  # Columns: County, r1403
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)  # Columns: County, r1402
df2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)  # Columns: County
df3 = pd.read_csv(source3_path, index_col=0)  # Columns: County, r1401

# Transformation plan:
# Target schema: ['County', 'r1401', 'r1403']
# Source tables:
# - df3 has r1401
# - df0 has r1403
# - df1 has r1402 (not needed in target)
# - df2 has only County (dimension table with more counties)
#
# We need to produce a table with County, r1401, r1403.
# We will join all sources on County to get all available data.
# r1402 is not part of target schema, so it will be ignored.
# df2 contains additional counties that might not appear in other sources.
# To cover all counties, we do a full outer join on County across all sources.
#
# Steps:
# 1. Merge df3 (County, r1401) with df0 (County, r1403) on County (outer join)
# 2. Merge the result with df2 (County only) on County (outer join) to add any missing counties
# 3. We do not use df1 (r1402) as it is not in target schema.
# 4. Fill missing r1401 and r1403 with 'NR' (consistent with source data)
# 5. Ensure columns are in target order: County, r1401, r1403
# 6. Sort by County alphabetically for neatness (optional)

# Merge df3 and df0 on County (outer join)
df_merged = pd.merge(df3, df0, on="County", how="outer")

# Merge with df2 (County only) to include all counties
df_merged = pd.merge(df_merged, df2, on="County", how="outer")

# After merge, df_merged columns: County, r1401, r1403
# Some rows may have NaN in r1401 or r1403, fill with 'NR'
df_merged['r1401'] = df_merged['r1401'].fillna('NR')
df_merged['r1403'] = df_merged['r1403'].fillna('NR')

# Select and reorder columns to match target schema
df_target = df_merged[['County', 'r1401', 'r1403']]

# Sort by County for consistent output
df_target = df_target.sort_values(by='County').reset_index(drop=True)

# Write the result to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_37/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_target.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
